chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Sonny Clay's later personnel, Ivie Anderson and the Creole Palace
summary: Ivie Anderson sang often at Spikes's theater before Ellington; Clay's unit played the Creole Palace in San Diego run by George Ramsey.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: "In January 1925 Paul Howard came into the band for a short period, replacing Charlie Mosley and giving the drummer at the time as Ben Borders. A year later trombonist Luther Graven commenced working with Clay."
And Ivie Anderson was working with Clay at the Vernon Country Club. Ivie worked around town a lot as a single...
She worked with different bands and...
Oh, yeah, before she got with Duke. Yeah. She worked with me a lots down to the theater down there, you know.
Eddie Nicholson, drums. Teddy Buckner. Red Mack, trumpet.

James Williams, trombone. Albert Baker, alto saxophone. And here's Leonard Davidson listed as "Big Boy." And Bert Holloway, tuba and string bass. Jimmy Warren, violin. And it says, "This unit was resident at the Creole Palace in San Diego..."
Well, of course, they were all from Los Angeles. Creole Palace, I think, was run by Ramsey, wasn't it? Does it say Ramsey?
I knew about the Creole Palace a little later on. In the '40s, I heard about the music there.
